steps: This video shows how one M C P server replaces copied tool code across apps. Three teams need the same Jira and C R M tools, and pasting a copy into each app means those copies drift apart.
Instead you build one M C P server with two narrow tools, jira create issue and crm lookup customer, spoken over J S O N R P C. It can run over standard I O, H T T P or S S E.
TicketFlow connects as an M C P client and calls tools list. The server returns two tools, each named mcp, server name, tool name, and TicketFlow adds them to its allowed tools.
The Escalation Dashboard and Analytics plug into the same server and call tools list too. They get the same two tools, with no new glue code.
When TicketFlow sends tools call, the server reaches the Jira A P I using a token from its environment. Credentials stay in the server, not in each app.
Jira answers that the issue is created, and the tool result returns to TicketFlow. TicketFlow treats that result as untrusted data and asks for approval before side effects.

Later you fix the Jira tool once, and the fix lands in all three apps. The takeaway: shared tools belong in M C P, private ones stay custom. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
